issues.title: TERNREF1: version-pinned, searchable, runtime-validated local reference for the Tern Plugin SDK
issues.description:
## Background
- Fleet plugin work leans on Tern Plugin SDK behaviour that is documented only online and partly only in the runtime. There is no pinned, searchable local copy, so agents guess or re-crawl.
- Pilot (2026-10-15, chief-claude) at `/Users/josh/Developer/omp-kit/var/agent-tmp/chief-claude.27434/terndocs/`:
  - **Sources:**
    - 165 pages crawled from https://docs.stencil.so/tern/index.html;
    - `tern plugin types` → `runtime/tern.d.luau` for tern 0.8.4 6b4535f;
    - 29 `tern <cmd> --help` files under `runtime/cli/`.
  - **Index:** corpus of 2,573 chunks (`corpus.jsonl` + `.manifest.json`); nomic index `idx-nomic`, verified (`verify.log`).
  - **Results:** 8 real queries gave 5 correct, 2 partial, 1 miss.
- Defects found:
  1. `print.html` duplicates every page (exclude it).
  2. The CLI help is too thin to answer usage questions alone.
  3. `tern.d.luau` was split by paragraph rather than per member.
  4. The embedding skill's crawler drops the start URL's trailing slash, so relative links 404. Workaround: start at `/tern/index.html`.
- Owner: the kit (omp-kit), not a project.

## Technical Approach
1. **Build command.** Promote the pilot's steps into one kit command in omp-kit-companion (proposed: `omp-kit tern-ref build|query|validate|drift`). Reuse the embedding skill's crawler and indexer (skill://embedding); do not write a new indexer. Fix the trailing-slash URL join upstream in that crawler, since it is the root cause, rather than keeping the workaround.
2. **Chunking rules:**
   - exclude `print.html`;
   - chunk `tern.d.luau` on top-level declarations (`declare`/`export type`/function members), carrying the parent type name;
   - enrich CLI help with the matching doc page section by command name.
3. **Storage.** Store everything under a kit-owned state dir keyed by `tern --version`, with a manifest: version, commit, per-source URL, ETag, sha256, chunk count, model.
4. **Retrieval eval.** Use a frozen `queries.jsonl` with expected source anchors. Run nomic and qwen. Collect blind labels from two model families (for example Claude plus Kimi or GLM via cheaper-inference) and compute kappa. Record the results in a dated receipt.
5. **Validate:**
   - write each claim as a scenario file (`run`/`expect`/`ready`);
   - launch `TERN_CONFIG_DIR=<scratch> tern serve --control <scratch>/ctl.sock` headless;
   - run the scenarios; tear down.
   - For omp surfaces, replay recordings with `surface-play`.
6. **Drift.** Conditional GET on ETags; compare `tern --version`. On change, re-index and diff chunk hashes. Then find beads citing changed chunk anchors (`br list --json` + text match) and report them. Do not mutate beads.

## Success Criteria
An agent can query a local, version-pinned SDK reference whose retrieval quality is measured, whose relied-on claims are proven against the real runtime in isolation, and which flags drift when the docs or the runtime change. Acceptance criteria above govern.

## Test Plan
Unit tests (in companion `tests/cli/tern-ref.test.ts`):
- the luau member chunker on a real `tern.d.luau` copy (asserting one chunk per member and parent names kept);
- `print.html` exclusion;
- URL join with and without a trailing slash (a **planted negative** that fails with today's crawler);
- manifest round-trip;
- drift diff on two manifests;
- the cited-bead matcher on a real `br list --json` fixture.

E2E: add `tests/e2e/tern-ref.e2e.sh`. It runs the public command:
- build → query (frozen set) → validate (scratch `tern serve`, including one planted false claim that must FAIL) → drift (a mutated ETag fixture).
- Per case it logs the fixture id and sha256, exact argv, exit code, expected vs observed disposition, and running totals. The final line is a JSON summary.
- It asserts that the socket and config dir live under `var/agent-tmp` and that the live daemon's socket was not touched.

Mutation check. The tests must kill each of these mutants:
- the planted false claim reported as pass;
- the version check skipped in drift;
- the luau chunker falling back to paragraph splitting.

## Considerations
- **Licensing and politeness:** the crawl is a local copy for internal use. Rate-limit it and honour ETags.
- **Runtime checks:** these require the installed `tern`. On a machine without it, validation reports UNAVAILABLE, never pass.
- **Scale:** the qwen index cost and size are larger. Pick a model on the measured result, not by default.
- **Out of scope:** general plugin docs for other SDKs, and auto-editing beads on drift.
- **Verifier:** a non-author from another model family replays the e2e and re-labels a sample of the queries.


Part of RC1016 (ompkit-fp72.120), milestone M6 (ompkit-fp72.120.7).
Plan: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_OMP_KIT.md §10 (ompkit-fp72.27)
issues.acceptance_criteria:
1. One kit command rebuilds the reference from source for the installed `tern --version`. It writes a manifest recording the tern version and commit, each page's URL, ETag and sha256, the chunk count, and the index model. Source pages: https://docs.stencil.so/tern/index.html crawl (`print.html` excluded), `tern plugin types` → `tern.d.luau` chunked **per declared member**, and each `tern <cmd> --help`.
2. Retrieval quality is measured on a frozen query set (≥ the 8 pilot queries, plus new ones), comparing nomic vs qwen. Labels are blind, from two model families, with Cohen's kappa reported. The chosen model must beat the pilot baseline (5 correct / 2 partial / 1 miss of 8). A regression fails the gate.
3. Each fleet-relied plugin claim becomes an executable check against the installed runtime. Checks run in an isolated headless `tern serve --control <scratch socket>` with its own `TERN_CONFIG_DIR` under `var/agent-tmp` (never the live daemon, never /tmp). Checks use the scenario commands (run/expect/ready) and `surface-play`. One planted false claim must fail.
4. Drift handling:
   - A changed ETag or `tern --version` triggers a re-index.
   - Beads citing changed chunks are listed. They are listed only and never auto-mutated.
5. Independent non-author replay.

issues.title: PRODUCTDEF1: define 'a finished, verified product' in the master plan - criteria with checkable evidence, App Store and Google Play end-to-end requirements as the floor, researched examples and negative examples
issues.description:
WHAT: write plan §0.1: the definition of a finished, verified product as criteria a non-author can check; the floor is everything Apple's App Store and Google Play require end to end (account, build, signing, privacy, review, release, post-release vitals); add researched software-release rigor beyond the stores; give a bank of examples and negative examples, each with its source; G4 and W7 test against it
WHY: Joshua (J-2026-10-19-91, -92): the mission says 'finished, verified product' without saying what that is; meeting the App Store and Google Play requirements end to end is the baseline to evolve from.

Plan: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_OMP_KIT.md §0.1, §11 G4 and W7. Research by background agents with cited primary sources (developer.apple.com, support.google.com/googleplay, developer.android.com, standards bodies); every requirement quoted from its source with URL and retrieval date.
issues.acceptance_criteria:
- [x] §0.1 lists each criterion with the evidence that proves it and the command or artifact a non-author checks; every App Store and Google Play requirement in the research tables maps to a criterion or is marked not applicable with a reason.
- [x] At least 12 examples and 12 negative examples, each citing a source (store rejection reason, policy text, postmortem or standard); planted negative: a product description missing one floor requirement is classified not finished by two non-claude graders using only §0.1.
- [x] G4 in §11 cites §0.1 as its acceptance.

- [ ] A rerun round by two non-claude families on the post-disposition plan reports 0 critical findings.

issues.title: PLANSYNC1: closes flow into the plan - generated status blocks with a parity check, a plan-delta producer with folds.jsonl dispositions, and a plan-debt command-center row
issues.description:
WHAT: build §16.1: (1) every count/progress/as-built table in the master plan is a <!-- gen:<producer> --> block regenerated from tracker, inventory and graph, with a parity check; (2) plan_delta.py lists beads closed since the plan's last revision by cited section with changed paths and new verbs/refusal codes/scripts the graph sees; (3) folds.jsonl records fold or 'no plan change: <reason>' per entry; (4) a plan_debt row (unfolded closes + unmapped components, oldest age) in the command center
WHY: Joshua (J-2026-10-19-83): beads close fast and their changes must reach the plan. Measured 22:30Z: graph has 2 plan nodes vs 900 beads; a 17-finding review sat undispositioned while §20 said round 0.

Plan: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_OMP_KIT.md §16 and §11 W0. Said log: J-2026-10-19-83. Stdlib, bounded, read-only on the tracker; commits under docs/plan/ and scripts/ with git commit --only and Bead: trailer. Not a close gate (gate admission order, design-out first).
issues.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] parity check exits 0 on the committed plan and 1 when a planted edit changes one number inside a gen block, naming the block; regenerating twice is byte-identical.
- [ ] plan_delta.py over a window lists every closed bead citing a plan section (count equals `br list --status closed` filtered by the same window and label, shown side by side); a planted close with a new verb appears with that verb; folds.jsonl entries remove it from the debt.
- [ ] plan_debt row present in the command center JSON with count and oldest age; planted unfolded close older than 24 h turns it red.

issues.title: PROCDRILL1: foreign and local runbook drills - a fresh agent with only the docs drives install, upgrade, rollback, restart, release dry run and planted-fault recovery
issues.description:
WHAT: run the §15 foreign drill (clean HOME, stock tools, only docs/runbooks/) and local drill (test profile, planted faults: killed seat, paused goal, stale index lock, full disk); every stumble becomes a doc fix and a rerun; record a drill receipt per runbook
WHY: a runbook nobody has followed from a clean start is a claim, not a procedure; the drill is the only proof that a foreign user can drive omp-kit.

Plan: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_OMP_KIT.md §15 and §11 W0. Said log: J-2026-10-19-82. Depends on PROCWRITE1. Graders are two non-author model families; the portable rows also run in CI on a stock runner.
issues.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Foreign drill PASS: P1-P4, P6-P8, R1 dry run, O5, O6, O10 with zero human messages, graded PASS by two non-author families; CI job on a stock runner green for the portable rows.
- [ ] Local drill PASS on every local row with the four planted faults recovered; each runbook carries a last-drill receipt id.
- [ ] Planted negative: deleting one step from a drilled runbook makes the drill fail at that step.

issues.title: PROCWRITE1: write the missing runbooks as RUNBOOK-SCHEMA data with a generated docs/runbooks/INDEX.md and a runbook lint
issues.description:
WHAT: for each catalog row whose gap list is not empty, write or fix its runbook (portable in docs/runbooks/, local addendum in the orchestration skill references/), add a runbook shape lint and generate INDEX.md
WHY: PROCINV1 lists the gaps; this closes them so the drill can run.

Plan: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_OMP_KIT.md §15 and §11 W0. Said log: J-2026-10-19-82. Depends on PROCINV1. One runbook per background agent in waves of up to 8.
issues.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every one of the 31 rows has a runbook; the shape lint exits 0 on all of them and INDEX.md regenerates byte-identically twice.
- [ ] Planted negatives: a runbook with no rollback, and one with a step that has no verify exit code, each make the lint exit 1 naming the file and field.

issues.title: PROCEDURES1: operator runbook ecosystem - every procedure (install, upgrade, rollback, release cut and tracking, restart, reboot recovery, incidents, backup) as runbook data a foreign or local user can drive with no gap
issues.description:
WHAT: build the §15 runbook ecosystem: one runbook per catalog row (P1-P9, R1-R4, O1-O13, G1-G5) as RUNBOOK-SCHEMA data, a generated index, and the five no-gap checks
WHY: Joshua (J-2026-10-19-82) wants any user, foreign or local, to pick up omp-kit and drive it immediately; today procedures are scattered over README, skill references, scripts and session memory, and none has a drill receipt.

Plan: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_OMP_KIT.md §15 and §11 W0. Said log: J-2026-10-19-82. Slices: inventory (phase A data), write (missing runbooks), drill (foreign and local).
issues.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] All five §15 no-gap checks pass twice on one commit: coverage 0 unmapped, shape lint 0 failures, foreign drill PASS by two non-author families with zero human help, local drill PASS, freshness 0 stale.
